newsitem.title: UK: Guinness says bought 44 mln shares at 414p.
newsitem.headline: Guinness says bought 44 mln shares at 414p.

text.p: Drinks group Guinness Plc said on Friday that it had purchased 44 million of its own ordinary shares in the market at a price of 414 pence during the day.
"The shares, which represent approximately 2.3 percent of its issued share capital, will be cancelled," the company said in a statement.
The transaction was worth about 182.16 million stg.
The shares were offered to Guinness through the marketplace as a result of French luxury goods company LVMH's decision to sell one third of its stake in Guinness.
"At this share price, Guinness would have bought the lot. But the placing was heavily oversubscribed so its allocation was scaled down by half to 2.3 percent," said one analyst close to the company.

Guinness has shareholder approval to buy back up to 10 percent of its shares (although it is prevented from doing so during the so-called close season which begins on Monday) ahead of its full year results due on March 20.

Analysts said they expect Guinness to buy back another five percent of its shares shortly after its full year results, especially if the share price remains at current levels -- their lowest since March 1995.
Guinness bought back 100 million shares in March 1996, about five percent of its share capital, at a cost of about 463 million pounds.

"Today's purchase is further demonstration of the company's continued committment to ensuring that its balance sheet is managed in the long term interests of its shareholders," said finance director Phil Yea in a statement.
Taken with the buyback executed last March and the dividends paid since then, Friday's purchase brings the cash returned to shareholders over the last year to 933 million, Yea said.
The company said advance corporation tax of about 30 million pounds will be payable on Friday's purchase which should be recovered in the fourth quarter of 1997.
